record.paper_title: 二分決定グラフに基づく計算複雑さに関する未解決問題について
record.original_question: Determine the relationship between l-LogCut and PolyTDD_SOP. Here l-LogCut is the class computed by polynomial-size circuit families whose graph cutwidth is O(log n), with each input bit represented by at most one input gate and with only linear arrangements in which the input gates appear in the prescribed order; PolyTDD_SOP is the class computed by polynomial-size ternary decision diagram families that represent sum-of-products formulas. Is one of these classes contained in the other, are they equal, or are they incomparable?

artifact.category_tag: Boolean circuit and decision diagram complexity
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions.

(a) A Boolean circuit on n input variables x_1,...,x_n is a directed acyclic graph whose sources (in‑degree 0) are labelled by input variables or constants ("input gates") and whose internal nodes are labelled by Boolean gates from a fixed finite basis. A linear arrangement of the circuit is a bijection of its nodes onto {1,2,...,N}; the cutwidth of a linear arrangement is the maximum, over all i, of the number of edges (u,v) with arrangement‑position(u) ≤ i < arrangement‑position(v). The graph cutwidth of the circuit is the minimum cutwidth over all linear arrangements.

(b) Let l-LogCut denote the class of Boolean functions f = (f_n)_{n≥1} such that there exists a family (C_n) of Boolean circuits of size polynomial in n computing f_n with the following properties:
   (i) each input variable x_i is read by at most one input gate of C_n;
   (ii) there exists a linear arrangement of C_n attaining cutwidth O(log n) in which the input gates appear in the prescribed order x_1, x_2, ..., x_n;
hence "l" indicates the restriction to such ordered linear arrangements with at most one input gate per variable.

(c) A ternary decision diagram (TDD) on variables x_1,...,x_n is a rooted directed acyclic graph in which every internal node is labelled by a variable and has exactly three outgoing edges labelled 0, 1, and *, and every sink is labelled 0 or 1. The function computed by a TDD is defined in the natural way, with the *-edge being followed when the label may be either 0 or 1. A TDD is said to represent a sum‑of‑products (SOP) formula F = T_1 ∨ T_2 ∨ ... ∨ T_m (each T_j a conjunction of literals) if its accepting paths from the root to the 1-sink, read as partial assignments via {0,1,*}, are exactly the terms T_1,...,T_m. Let PolyTDD_SOP denote the class of Boolean functions computed by families (D_n) of TDDs of size polynomial in n that represent some sum‑of‑products formula for the function.

Question. Determine the inclusion relationship between the classes l-LogCut and PolyTDD_SOP. Specifically, decide whether l-LogCut ⊆ PolyTDD_SOP, whether PolyTDD_SOP ⊆ l-LogCut, whether the two classes coincide, or whether they are incomparable.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the relationship between the l-LogCut class (polynomial-size circuits of O(log n) cutwidth with ordered input gates) and PolyTDD_SOP (polynomial-size ternary decision diagrams representing sum-of-products formulas) could be located. The question appears to be stated as an open problem in the literature on BDD-based complexity, and no subsequent work establishing inclusion, equality, or incomparability was found.
